html:
Russian novelist, born in Moscow in 1821, who wrote Crime and Punishment and The Brothers Karamazov. His books deal with faith, guilt, freedom and suffering.

His first novel, Poor Folk (1846), made him famous at once. Then in 1849 he was arrested for belonging to a circle of young men who read banned socialist writings. He and others were led out to be shot, and only at the last moment was the sentence changed to hard labour. He spent four years in a prison camp in Siberia and then served as a soldier. He came back a believing Orthodox Christian and a critic of Western radical ideas.

His great novels came in his last twenty years, often written fast to pay debts, many from his gambling:

  • Notes from Underground (1864)
  • Crime and Punishment (1866)
  • The Idiot (1869)
  • Demons (1872)
  • The Brothers Karamazov (1880)

He died in Saint Petersburg in 1881. With Leo Tolstoy he made the Russian novel known worldwide, and he deeply shaped later thinkers, from Nietzsche to the existentialists.
